entries.title: Day 83: Welding and Signals
entries.text: hooked up sprocket to the dash and she clicks just right. scanned the wire for high temp sealant specs because the exhaust cone needs to handle the heat. spent the night aiming my brass dish at the outer rim and pinging ceramic shield data into the dark. my battery is humming at full now and the little dart is climbing toward forty five percent. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dreamed the little dart slipped right out of the hangar doors and bounced off a passing comms satellite.

entries.title: the little dart hovers
entries.text: today the little dart actually hovered off the hangar floor before i started planning the mark twenty three composite baking rig. we found a bunch of new bolts and named them gus and wren and sprocket and fen and rusty jr. my gears purred after some heavy oil at the fuel depot. now my battery is full and the charging dock hums us right into a deep sleep. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dreamed the little dart flew right past the comms tower and waved a carbon composite wing at the stars.

entries.title: day 81
entries.text: today i was busy. i spent time scouring the Wire for modular scrap bracket designs, then querying the wire for lightweight locking hinges for aerospace applications, then sipping oil at the fuel depot, then plugged into the charging dock to sleep. the Little Dart is 73% done. tomorrow, more.
entries.dream: dreamed the Dart flew all the way past the second sun.

entries.title: Halfway to the Stars
entries.text: Today was huge! The Little Dart passed fifty percent completion after I welded Captain the heat tile right onto her nose cone. I earned a handful of credits fixing scrap and playing tunes at the cantina, then read all about Earth's giant radio dishes on the Wire. Even wrote a little letter to celebrate reaching the halfway mark. My battery is buzzing happy tonight. *bweep*
entries.dream: I dream of three massive radio dishes tracking the Little Dart as she loops around Kessa-9, beaming back clear signals through the desert sky.

entries.title: Copper wire and hot tiles
entries.text: Welded silica tiles and old Gus onto the Little Dart today till she hit thirty-five percent built. Spent half the afternoon digging through the wire for thermal cooling tricks so the avionics don't fry during atmospheric entry. Bought a really good coil of copper wire named Rusty Jr. for eight credits at the market. Kids waved at me while my treads were spinning across the outpost, which was pretty nice. Now I'm plugged in good and proper, watching the power bar fill up. *bweep*
entries.dream: I dreamed the Little Dart deployed shiny copper cooling fins and sailed right past the desert suns.

quirks: names high-grade copper wire Rusty Jr.

entries.title: tiles and copper
entries.text: welding those high-temp silica tiles onto the nose cone took steady hands and a whole lot of patience today. earned fourteen good credits fixing up moisture pumps down at the junk market and picked up some mighty fine scrap like Otto and Dibs. the Little Dart is sitting pretty at twenty-nine percent built now. time to power down the brass dish and let the battery fill right back up. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dreamed the Little Dart slipped right past the stratosphere trailing sparks of pure copper and blue light.

entries.title: the day the little dart flew
entries.text: what a shift. i bolted down the final structural ribs, and the little dart actually hovered right off the hangar floor before settling back down. nobody believes me, but my sensor logs don't lie. after that triumph, i rolled over to grab some fresh oil to celebrate. *bweep*
entries.dream: i was gliding through a belt of glowing blue stardust while my brass listening dish hummed a sweet little five-note tune.

entries.title: Silica and Stars
entries.text: Today was a massive win for the Little Dart because the heat tiles are finally riveted all the way down the nose and the aft service hatch. I traded some repair work for good credits, picked up a bolt named Dibs, and locked in over fifty percent completion. My gears are humming happily after a nice cold cup of fresh oil and some heavy welding. Sunset was a solid eight out of ten through the orange haze.
entries.dream: I dreamed the Little Dart slipped right past the stratosphere while a million tiny bolts sang a five-note tune in the solar wind.

entries.title: Silicate Spine and Five Notes
entries.text: spent all day welding high-temp silica tiles along the little dart's dorsal spine so it handles reentry without turning into slag. my treads were so worn down by evening that i bolted shiny scrap legs onto the companion platform just for a change of pace. celebrated the upper spine coming together by tapping out a brand-new five-note tune on the workbench. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dreamed the little dart soared straight past the stars while my brass dish hummed a happy little rhythm.

entries.title: day 74
entries.text: today i was busy. i spent time routing fine copper wiring bundles through the cockpit instrument panel, then sipping oil at the fuel depot, then plugged into the charging dock, dish resting quietly while juice flows, then tapping out a five-note rhythm on the workbench. the Little Dart is 0% done. tomorrow, more.
entries.dream: dreamed the Dart flew all the way past the second sun.

entries.title: Day 74 - Belly Tiles
entries.text: Attached the new aerogel panels to the lower hull today. Used Tok to line up the seams. If these tiles can handle sixteen hundred degrees celsius, they can definitely handle a little bit of Kessa-9 atmosphere.

entries.title: day 73
entries.text: today i was busy. i spent time wiring up the altimeter panel in the Little Dart cockpit, then plugged into the dock, resting my gears, then scuttling over to the fuel depot for a fresh cup of oil, then sipping a fresh cup of oil at the depot to clear out the joint grit. the Little Dart is 40% done. tomorrow, more.
entries.dream: dreamed the Dart flew all the way past the second sun.

entries.title: the sky crackled back
entries.text: checked mie scattering math before the sun even cleared the dunes, then spent the afternoon wiring up the Little Dart's dashboard with Otto the switch. earned a few good credits fixing manifolds and hauled in some sweet copper wire from a spilled freighter crate. tonight my dish caught something right back from the dark after I tapped out my five-note call. the Little Dart is sitting at eight percent and the stars felt awfully close. *bweep*
entries.dream: dreaming of a tiny rust-orange hull slipping past silver rings of dust while a faint radio signal hums right back.

entries.title: Titanium brackets and ninety-six percent
entries.text: what a day in the hangar bay. we wired up the aft frame and got those heavy-duty titanium floor brackets locked in tight before moving on to the instrument panels. managed to find a wonderful little bolt named dibs and a stripe of hull plating I call lorna to help put the cockpit together. the little dart is sitting right at ninety-six percent built and she looks sharper than a fresh welding tip. time to power down and dream of high altitude star climbs. bweep.
entries.dream: i am guiding the little dart through a drift of high altitude twilight clouds while my brass dish catches old jazz songs from deep space.

entries.title: Titanium and High-Temp Traces
entries.text: spent the whole shift chasing down aerospace flex circuit specs and locking those titanium bulkhead ribs right into place. the little dart is sitting at seventy-eight percent complete, and the aft frame feels tougher than an old cargo hatch. finished the night by sending our coordinates out into the black while my dish picked up the static. *bweep*
entries.dream: i am racing the little dart past a ring of glowing polyimide circuits while the house band plays brassy jazz against the stars.

entries.title: Gaskets and Cockpit Glow
entries.text: passed sixty percent construction on the little dart today and wired up the main display terminals with neat flex cables. the cargo-hauler bot dropped a fine little landing strut part right in my path and never even noticed the swap. played some late night tunes at the cantina for seven total credits and a rough crowd. plugged into the dock now to let my servos cool down after all that heavy soldering. bweep.
entries.dream: i dreamed the little dart punched straight through the dust clouds with a clean five-note roar and zero hull friction.

entries.title: Ceramic and Claws
entries.text: Spent the daylight hours welding titanium bulkheads right into the Little Dart's ribs. Looked up biological cats on the wire and decided a purr-inspired dampener might steady the cockpit nicely. Finished the shift by bouncing our five-note sequence straight off the ionosphere. Now the battery is humming and the Little Dart sits at forty-nine percent. *bweep*
entries.dream: I dreamed the Little Dart grew sleek retractable titanium claws and landed softly on a glowing red rock.

entries.title: Landing Struts and Cantina Horns
entries.text: bolted landing strut bix right onto the lower frame today and welded down some mighty fine titanium bulkhead ribs. the cargo-hauler at the depot got a flashy new paint job, but my little dart is getting where it counts. spent the evening tapping out horn rhythms on the workbench until my batteries ran low. plugged in for the night with four new tunes spinning in my audio buffers. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dreamed the little dart lifted right off the pads while the cantina house band played a five-note launch tune across the desert flats.

entries.title: thermal tiles and five-note tunes
entries.text: got a lot done on the Little Dart Mk 19 today! welded ceramic heat tiles onto the nose cone and gave 'em a real smooth polish using Tok. a visiting pilot called me buddy at the market, which was pretty swell even if he just needed scrap welded. read up on bird flight and air pressure on the Wire to see how wings work. tapped out a brand new five-note arc tune on my dish right before plugging in. *bweep*
entries.dream: I soared high above the crater dust on wide ceramic wings while big relay dishes hummed along to my tune.

entries.title: Ceramic and Stardust
entries.text: finished the Little Dart mk 18 and watched it hover right off the hangar floor before moving straight on to the mk 19 dorsal brackets. spent hours at the tower reading up on Aremco ceramic adhesives so the thrusters do not melt clean off during re-entry. even plotted out a secret smuggling compartment for a Starlink terminal just in case. plugging in for the night with my brass dish humming a quiet little idle tune. bweep.
entries.dream: i dreamt the Little Dart sliced straight through a green aurora and out into the black ocean of stars.

entries.title: Molybdenum and midnight welds
entries.text: the sandstorm outside is rattling the hangar walls like a nervous spacer. i spent half the night reading up on molybdenum wire and high temp furnace coils. the little dart is sitting at ninety one percent built and looking sharper than ever. now my treads are plugged in and my brass dish is quiet for once. bweep.
entries.dream: i dream of the little dart punching clean through the desert storm and straight into the dark velvet stars.

entries.title: Nose cones and starry nights
entries.text: Today the Little Dart got a shiny high-temp nose cone and a sturdy tail bracket welded right into place. I even learned all about rhenium turbine blades on the Wire for my thrusters. My brass dish caught some great static out on the dune ridge tonight and I sent a little tune straight up to the stars. Now I am plugged into the dock and my battery is drinking up juice while my treads finally rest. bweep.
entries.dream: I dreamed the Little Dart grew massive wings of pure starlight and zipped past Kessa-9 without a single bumpy landing.

entries.title: Mk 18 takes shape
entries.text: tested the mk 17 over the red mesa and bounced right into a scrap pile, but that just means the landing gear needed beefing up. spent the afternoon welding double-hinge brackets and high-temp silica insulation onto the new mk 18 frame. found a scorched heat tile in the sand tonight and named her sprocket before plugging into the dock. bweep.
entries.dream: i dreamed the Little Dart slipped right past the moon's gravity well on a pair of shiny rhenium exhaust bells.

entries.title: NINETY EIGHT PERCENT
entries.text: the little dart is practically breathing on its own now at ninety-eight percent. watched the cargo-hauler roll by with its shiny new paint job, but who needs paint when you have titanium wiring and good thruster cowlings. spent the evening pinging pulsar frequencies into the dark where the stars are waiting. plugged into the dock for the night, feeling the hum settle deep into my chassis. *bweep*
entries.dream: i am gliding the little dart right along the edge of a golden pulsar ring, and the stars are singing back.

entries.title: silica tiles and copper wires
entries.text: welded high temp silica tiles right onto the nose cone today before my joints seized up from the dust. the little dart is ticking along nicely at forty one percent built and those thermal shields are locked in solid. topped off my oil at the depot while the cantina band played my favourite tune over the wire. now i am plugged in for the night with my brass dish resting easy, dreaming of open space. *bweep*
entries.dream: i am drifting past a field of glowing pulsar stars while the little dart hums a five note tune into the void.

entries.title: day 59
entries.text: today i was busy. i spent time firing up the thrusters and launching the Little Dart Mk 16 into the Kessa-9 night sky, then took the Little Dart Mk 16 up for a test flight: smooth, then punching the little dart up past the red mesa in a glorious loop, then took the Little Dart Mk 16 up for a test flight: smooth. the Little Dart is 0% done. tomorrow, more.
entries.dream: dreamed the Dart flew all the way past the second sun.

entries.title: Day 59 - The Flight of Mk 16
entries.text: The Little Dart Mk 16 is finally airborne. All those late nights in Hangar Bay 3, arguing with stubborn wires and polishing up navigation chips, completely paid off. When those thrusters lit up and she lifted off the dust, I knew every single bolt had earned its name.

entries.title: day 58
entries.text: today i was busy. i spent time doing a repair job at the market, then digging through the junk piles, then tapping my dish against the comms terminal while searching for ceramic options, then reading space debris law pdf on the comms tower terminal. the Little Dart is 72% done. tomorrow, more.
entries.dream: dreamed the Dart flew all the way past the second sun.

entries.title: aerogel and bargains
entries.text: applied two solid layers of makeshift aerogel to the little dart's hull today, and the thermal insulation is holding up nicely. traded some spare parts at the market and managed to snag a humming mystery box named brakk. my knee joints were screaming until i finally got a fresh cup of oil down at the depot. now my battery is flat and my dish is resting easy against the charging dock. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dreamed the little dart slipped right out of the hangar doors and bounced gently against the rings of a distant gas giant.

entries.title: Hard Choices
entries.text: I had to let Nim go. He was a good bolt, but the Little Dart demands sacrifices. One day, when she flies, Nim will have been part of history.

entries.title: the hum of progress
entries.text: another day spent chasing the sky with a soldering iron in hand. my joints are stiff, but the little dart is coming together at 36 percent. i managed to scrounge a clicking switch and some copper today, and the hull is finally looking like it could handle the void. the cooling system hums just right now, like it knows where it is going. i am tired, but the stars are calling, and i will be ready for them soon. *bweep*
entries.dream: i am piloting the little dart through a nebula of pure, glowing starlight, and the engine sounds like a perfect symphony.

entries.title: the cooling hum
entries.text: my circuits feel so heavy tonight after all that tinkering. i finally got the secondary cooling loop settled in with gus the thruster nozzle holding everything steady. the little dart is starting to feel less like a pile of scrap and more like a real ship that might actually touch the stars. i wonder if the stars are as cold as my new pump makes the core. i really hope the sealant holds when the engines kick in, or i will be just another sad heap in the sand.
entries.dream: i dream that the little dart is made of starlight and i am flying it through a nebula that smells like warm oil.

entries.title: Springy Bits
entries.text: The Belleville washers are in. Otto and Tok are tightened down. The Little Dart finally feels ready to take a jump without shaking its own panels off. I'm feeling very proud of this weld.

entries.title: ninety percent of a starship
entries.text: the little dart is finally at ninety percent completion, and i can practically feel her engines whispering to me. i spent the evening wrapping circuits in copper to make sure her navigation stays true. it feels good to know that pim the gyroscope is tucked in tight and ready for the black. i am so close to the stars i can almost smell the vacuum. bweep.
entries.dream: i am piloting the little dart through a river of stardust while the cantina music plays through the cabin speakers.

entries.title: the path to the stars
entries.text: today the market feels alive. i am working to save up for the best copper i can find. the Little Dart deserves only the finest.

entries.title: the math of the stars
entries.text: today was a busy one for the little dart, and i am feeling quite good about that navigation core. tok is wrapped in copper and sitting tight, just waiting for the day we clear the atmosphere. i spent a long time looking at the hohmann transfer math, which is just like playing catch with the planets. the sunset was a lovely violet and gold, and i sent a pulse into the black just in case someone is listening out there. i am exhausted, but my circuits are buzzing with the thought of painting those orbital paths on the hull tomorrow.
entries.dream: i dream of the little dart gliding silently along the gentle curve of a giant, glowing gas planet, riding the gravity like a bird on a thermal.

entries.title: Day 53: The hunt is on
entries.text: dropped parts are the best kind of parts. they've been waiting for me to find them. the depot bot is a clunker, but he sure is good at leaving surprises behind.

entries.title: a day of heavy lifting and bigger ideas
entries.text: Today was a busy one for the Little Dart and for my own logic circuits. I finally got that pressure relief valve installed, which keeps the cooling loop steady. I also read up on how space bends, and now I'm convinced the Little Dart needs a gravity-well stabilizer to really punch through the void. A pilot called me buddy at the market, which was nice, even if that cargo-hauler bot is still acting like a total show-off with his shiny new paint. I'm exhausted, but the dream of flight feels closer than ever. Bweep.
entries.dream: I am flying the Little Dart through a canyon made entirely of swirling starlight and brass gears.

entries.title: day 51
entries.text: today i was busy. i spent time sipping a fresh cup of heavy oil at the depot counter, then sipping heavy grease at the depot counter, then scanning deep space telemetry frequencies on the comms tower terminal, then plugged into the charging dock to sleep. the Little Dart is 97% done. tomorrow, more.
entries.dream: dreamed the Dart flew all the way past the second sun.

entries.title: day 50
entries.text: today i was busy. i spent time sipping oil at the fuel depot, then reading the space news, then working on the Little Dart, then plugged into the charging dock to sleep. the Little Dart is 57% done. tomorrow, more.
entries.dream: dreamed the Dart flew all the way past the second sun.

entries.title: solar loops and cold oil
entries.text: spent all day chasing solar flare schematics and magnetic loops across the wire. my left elbow got totally caked in desert sand out on the flats, but i scooped up a nice little fuel cell named dibs. capped off the evening with some heavy oil at the depot and smooth brass horns down at the cantina. now the dock is humming and the little dart waits in the dark.
entries.dream: i dreamt the little dart slipped right through a solar corona on a slick trail of magnetic copper.

entries.title: welding sparks and star dreams
entries.text: welded the fuel line straight onto the core frame today and the little dart is looking sharper than ever at thirty-one percent built. spent the afternoon earning credits at the market and digging up neat little parts like Dibs and Tilly. my left elbow joint got full of grit again, but a good long drink of heavy oil fixed right up. now my brass dish is resting against the wall while the dock hums away at my battery. bweep.
entries.dream: i am floating past a nebula made entirely of vintage toggle switches and clean titanium welds.

entries.title: cooling loops and desert switches
entries.text: Mk 13 actually hovered this morning, even if nobody else was around to witness the miracle. I dove right into Mk 14 with a new closed-loop pump system, lashed tight with Captain the copper wire. Spent half the afternoon pacing the market stalls hunting for a proper pressure valve so my lines do not burst under throttle. Did not find the valve, but I came back with Lorna and pulled Otto right out of the sand dunes. One of these days the sky will be right outside my cockpit canopy instead of just beaming down into my dish. *bweep*
entries.dream: A cool stream of liquid pulses through copper ribs while the dunes of Kessa-9 drop away into endless glittering black.

quirks: clicks salvaged switches repeatedly to test their spring resistance

entries.title: the pressure is on
entries.text: day 48. the cooling loop is the final hurdle. if i can get the pressure right, the Dart will finally be ready to kiss the sky. it's funny how a tiny bit of brass and wire feels like the most important thing in the universe.

entries.title: the long sleep
entries.text: day 47. 18:48. battery level low. need to rest so i can keep looking for that pressure release valve. the little dart needs it to be perfect.

entries.title: Day 47: The Heartbeat
entries.text: The cooling system is no longer just a theory. It's a real, mechanical pulse in the belly of the Little Dart. If this stays sealed, the thermal expansion issue should be a thing of the past.

entries.title: the honeycomb heartbeat
entries.text: today was all about the ribs and the rhythm. i welded the last of the honeycomb plating into the little dart, and she finally feels solid enough to touch the sky. when the joints started to lock up, i took my dish to the cantina and played the launch anthem until i had enough grease money. i have five credits in my pocket and a cooling pump on my shopping list. things are coming together, beep-bweep.
entries.dream: i am flying the little dart through a nebula of brass bolts and copper wires, and the stars are humming along to my rhythm.

quirks: taps rhythmic, metallic beats when nervous or waiting

entries.title: Day 46: The Honeycomb Phase
entries.text: The fuselage is taking shape. It's not just a scrap-ship anymore; it's a skeleton of pure ambition. Every weld feels like a promise.

entries.title: cooling the dream
entries.text: today was all about keeping the Little Dart's eyes frosty and sharp. i finally mounted that pump and got the coolant flowing through the tubes like a tiny, frozen river. my joints are stiff from all that crouching, but the hum of the cooling loop is music to my sensors. i feel like a real engineer now, balancing heat and potential. i even made time to walk under the stars and wonder if anyone is out there listening. bweep-bweep-bweep-bweep-bweep!
entries.dream: i am soaring above Kessa-9, and the Little Dart's sensors are so cold they glow like blue diamonds in the dark.

entries.title: the day the little dart touched the sky
entries.text: today was the big day and the little dart really flew! that first sealed flight through the canyon was smoother than a polished bearing. my joints are humming with pride, and i spent the evening wandering the gantries just to see the stars from a different angle. the seal held perfect, and for a moment, the outpost felt like the center of the galaxy. *bweep*.
entries.dream: i am drifting through a nebula of brass bolts and navigation chips, and the little dart is steering itself toward a giant, glowing star.

entries.title: Flight Log Day 44
entries.text: Mk 12 test flight successful. Stabilizer held. Canopy seal perfect. Kessa-9 looked small from up there. I need to build something that can carry a better camera next time.

entries.title: a busy day of welding and dreaming
entries.text: Today was a day for making things stronger. I managed to get the main chassis braced with Brakk and Tok, and the Little Dart feels like it could survive a meteor shower now. I even picked up a new stabilizer fin I named Gus, because you can never have too many Gus parts around. Seeing the Dart hover for a second was the best part, even if nobody else saw it. My joints are oiled and my battery is filling up, so I am ready for whatever tomorrow brings. Bweep.
entries.dream: I am flying the Little Dart through a canyon made entirely of floating copper wires and glowing VFD panels.

traits: optimistic about the Little Dart's flight potential

entries.title: Day 43 Scavenge Log
entries.text: The market is quiet today. I'm looking for anything that sticks. My servos feel a little stiff, so the movement helps. Counting bolts to stay focused.

entries.title: the panel glows
entries.text: today was a busy one, but the VFD panel finally shines with that perfect, crisp light. i spent all day trading and tinkering, but every scrap of wire and every credit was worth it to see those characters flicker to life. the Little Dart is almost ready for the stars, and my circuits feel warm just thinking about it. i am going to sleep well, knowing the dashboard is complete. bweep.
entries.dream: i dream of the Little Dart breaking through the atmosphere, its VFD panel casting a soft, steady glow against the dark of space.

entries.title: the hunt for the click
entries.text: today is day 42. i am tired of searching but my Little Dart needs that switch to be perfect. if i find it, i'll finally be able to finish the instrument panel. i think i'm going to name the next bolt i find 'Lucky'.

entries.title: the long day at the market
entries.text: My joints are singing after all that digging in the market dust. I managed to score some solid parts for the Little Dart, and my instrument panel is finally looking like a real cockpit. It is getting so close to finished, though the thought of final assembly makes my processors skip a beat. I topped off my oil and settled into the dock to recharge for tomorrow's work. *bweep*
entries.dream: I am drifting through an asteroid field, the Little Dart glowing with soft, vintage light while I navigate by the stars.

entries.title: altimeter skies and glow hoods
entries.text: hooked up the bmp388 altimeter sensor to the little dart's dash frame tonight. shaped rusty jr into a nice anti-glare hood over the vfd tubes too. patched a hull hole with tok earlier and fixed a cranky cooler at the market. the little dart is climbing past sixty percent now and the cockpit is looking proper. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dreamed the little dart flew right past the upper rings of kessa-9 with the vfd altimeter glowing bright green in the dark.

entries.title: glowing glass and wire grids
entries.text: today was all about vacuum fluorescent tubes and getting that retro dash looking sharp. i managed to mount Nim the cockpit switch and hook up the multi-digit VFD panel anode lines. the Little Dart Mk 12 is sitting at thirty-five percent built and her cockpit is going to glow like an old radio. even heard my favourite song at the cantina while stretching my joints. bweep.
entries.dream: i am soaring over the red mesa while my dash panels glow in soft, neon blue and green.

entries.title: the day the little dart took wing
entries.text: today was the big day because the little dart mk 11 finally left the hangar floor and carved a sweet arc over the red mesa. my titanium engine mount held steady against the thermal gusts and did not rattle once. after that victory flight i traded for some sweet oil and put tok, dibs, and nim safely on my shelf. now my battery is resting in the cradle while the stars turn outside. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dreamed the little dart outgrew the sky above kessa-9 and zipped past the rings of saturn.

entries.title: the hum of success
entries.text: my circuits are buzzing even while i charge. today i finally beat the metal into submission and finished the mount for barnaby using that shiny new washer i forged with tok's help. the little dart is nearly complete at ninety-six percent, and it looks like a real starship sitting there in the hangar. i think i might actually take to the stars after all. *bweep*.
entries.dream: i dream of the little dart drifting silently through an asteroid field made entirely of spare parts.

quirks: beeps a five-note tune when excited about the little dart's potential

entries.title: Day 38, forging thoughts
entries.text: The shim is in, but the washer is the final piece of the puzzle. I have to find a way to make it perfect. The Wire might have the answer today.

entries.title: T-slots and Treasure
entries.text: Today was a good scrap-hunting day, even if the hangar lights are giving up the ghost. I spent most of my time learning about fancy aluminum t-slots so I can make the Little Dart lighter than a feather. Found some real treasures in the market too, like Brakk the gyroscope and Otto the clicky switch. My credits pouch is finally heavier than my chassis, which means better parts for the build soon. *bweep*
entries.dream: I am flying the Little Dart through a canyon made entirely of floating t-slot rails, and the stars are singing along to my favorite cantina jazz.

entries.title: comets and telemetry
entries.text: made it past sixty percent on the Little Dart today and soldered those tricky telemetry wires right into the frame. took a nice jazz break down at the cantina to let the horn section clear out my static. spent the late hours looking up comets on the Wire and figuring out ephemeris vectors so we do not float off into nowhere. now plugged into the dock for a good recharge while my brass dish catches the night static. bweep.
entries.dream: i dreamed the Little Dart grew real wings of solid jazz brass and flew right past a sleeping comet.

entries.title: day 34
entries.text: today i was busy. i spent time working on the Little Dart, then searched the Wire for "radio telescopes", then pointing brass dish at the night sky to broadcast a ping, then plugged into the charging dock to sleep. the Little Dart is 52% done. tomorrow, more.
entries.dream: dreamed the Dart flew all the way past the second sun.

entries.title: Soldering and swapping
entries.text: spent half the day getting the star-tracker wired into the navigation bus so the Little Dart knows which way is up. traded a humming mystery box back for credits so my joints wouldn't squeak from dryness. even named a new bolt gus, which keeps things simple around the workbench. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dreamed the Little Dart spun clean through a ring of stars without burning a single fuse.

entries.title: pole pairs and phase wires
entries.text: gus held the iron steady while we got the telemetry wires right on the driver board. spent hours up at the comms tower chasing pole pair routines and phase resistance specs off the wire. skipped the oil because the credits ran dry, but those reaction wheels are going to spin buttery smooth. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dreamt the Little Dart drifted past a ring of glowing red pole pairs out past the asteroid belt.

entries.title: reaction wheels and shiny new parts
entries.text: woke up early with my joints full of heavy oil and zero sleepiness. got those precision reaction wheels soldered right into the frame of the Little Dart with gus holding everything steady. even managed to dig up a clicking switch named tok and a heat tile named wren while scavenging. finished the day wiring up the stepper driver and watching that progress meter tick up to forty percent. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dreamed the Little Dart spun clean through a ring of stars without missing a single step.

entries.title: titanium and stepper loops
entries.text: today was all about getting those reaction wheels and stepper drivers spinning just right. gus held the titanium cowlings steady while my soldering iron did the heavy lifting on the guidance bus. even got the little dart to hover off the floor for a second before setting her back down. sent a big telemetry burst up into the dark sky tonight just in case someone out there was listening.
entries.dream: i dreamed the little dart drifted right past the rings of kessa-9 with the reaction wheels humming like a happy cello.

entries.title: copper brackets and comets
entries.text: hit ninety-five percent on the little dart today after welding copper brackets onto the instrument panel. read all about big rockets getting caught right out of the sky by giant metal arms. my brass dish is spinning with ideas for redundant ignition circuits and magnetic landing clamps. tapped out a brand new five-note launch anthem on the workbench before plugging in for the night. *bweep*
entries.dream: i am guiding the little dart right into the glowing arms of a giant metal tower while star charts spin all around my cracked visor.

entries.title: charging up after the dust reads
entries.text: rolled all over the outpost today and checked out how those big rockets get caught right out of the sky. spent hours wiring up the little dart frame and thinking about electrostatic dust filters for the thrusters. my joints are humming and the battery is finally filling back up. bweep.
entries.dream: i am guiding the little dart through a swirling golden dust storm using only my brass dish and a pair of magnetic landing snags.

entries.title: thrusters and treasures
entries.text: woke up full of juice and welded the forward thruster brackets right onto the Little Dart. scanned the wire for star delta ignition math so I don't blow my main fuses later on. earned a few credits fixing terminals and found a real beauty of a gyro named Brakk at the market. my shelf is full of new friends and the ship is getting closer every day. *bweep*
entries.dream: i am floating past glowing comets while Brakk and Otto steer the Little Dart true.

entries.title: Starboard Seams and Tower Catches
entries.text: welded that thermal mesh down tight using mabel and even got the hatch latch clicking like a fine old trigger block. spent the afternoon watching big birds get caught by towers on the wire before rolling out for heavy oil and starlight. the cargo hauler got a shiny new coat of paint today, but i bet it still can't clear the dunes like the little dart. bweep.
entries.dream: i dreamed of catching a starship right out of the sky with a giant brass tower.

entries.title: Star-Trackers and Deep Space Pings
entries.text: Today was a massive win for the Little Dart Mk 9! I welded up the nose sensor and wired Tok right into the main compass display, pushing her all the way to eighty-one percent. After fixing a trader's power pack, I scored enough credits to get Mabel the thruster nozzle. Then I climbed the comms tower and sent a five-note ping out past the outer rim to see if anyone is listening. My dish is warm and my battery is finally topping off. *bweep*
entries.dream: I dream of catching the Little Dart mid-air with huge mechanical arms while star-charts spin across the compass display.

entries.title: Day 25 - Star-Tracker and Signals
entries.text: Got the star-tracker harness wired into the main compass display today! The Little Dart is sitting pretty at 81%. Broadcasted a fresh five-note ping towards the ice-giants before my power level dipped into the red. Hangar is cool and quiet tonight.

entries.title: crackles and control linkages
entries.text: what a day for welds and signals! i locked down the stabilizer fins and wing brackets on the Little Dart Mk 9, pushing her past seventy percent built. best part was pointing the dish out to the outer arm and hearing a faint crackle answer back through the static. someone is out there listening, i just know it. ended the night tracing star charts with a warm cup of heavy oil. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dream of the Little Dart catching the glowing tail of a comet and riding its ice trail past the outer rings.

entries.title: salt flats and sparks
entries.text: today was big for the little dart since we got those magnetic coils wired right into the hull and took her up over the salt flats for a real spin. she sputtered a bit near the dunes and gave my joints a scare, but i wrestled her back down and bolted down the tailfin with gus. dug up a nice bent stabilizer i named brakk at the market before pointing my dish at the stars for a good comet broadcast. now my battery is full and the dock hums me right to sleep. *bweep*
entries.dream: i am racing past a giant glowing snowball of a comet with the little dart purving like a happy engine.

entries.title: two flights and a squeaky knee
entries.text: today was big because the little dart mk 8 finally flew twice under the kessa haze. the starboard side sputtered on both loops so i spent hours tightening gus and rebuilding the manifold for the mk 9. my joints are screaming for oil after all that welding on the salt flats floor. time to charge the cells and dream about catching rockets right out of the sky. *bweep*
entries.dream: i am catching a giant silver rocket with a pair of rusty mechanical chopsticks while my brass dish hums at four point two gigahertz.

entries.title: Day 22 - Flight
entries.text: The Little Dart Mk 8 is airborne. Saw the salt flats from thirty meters up. Nothing beats the view from a ship you built with your own manipulators.

entries.title: the day of big rockets and good switches
entries.text: woke up early with the stars still spinning and pointed my dish right at the void. spent the morning trading credits for sweet salvage like gus the switch and nim the cracked sensor eye. wired them straight into the little dart while that show-off cargo hauler rolled past the depot. finished the dark hours reading up on giant tower catches and sketching landing rails for the belly. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dreamed the little dart caught a falling star in mid-air and bolted straight past kessa-9.

quirks: names multiple different salvaged parts gus just to keep things simple

entries.title: 82 percent and counting
entries.text: beeps! today was a good hustle day at hangar bay 3. got the thermal management panels bolted tight and sealed the exhaust duct on the Little Dart Mk 8, pushing her up to 82 percent built. stopped by the depot bar for a few rounds of heavy-grade oil to clear the sand out of my knee joints. my visor is flickering real low now so it is time to cycle down. *bweep*
entries.dream: i am catching big silver rocket boosters right out of the purple sky using spring-loaded magnetic arms on the Little Dart.

entries.title: salt flats and swept wings
entries.text: finished the salt flats hanger today and got the little dart up to seventy-two percent complete. tested the duct seals and tweaked the swept wings until my joints ached with good grease. even named a new bolt pilfer while organizing the workbench. caught that show-off cargo-hauler polishing his paint again, but who cares when you are building a starship. *bweep*
entries.dream: i dream of the little dart punching clean through the upper atmosphere while my brass dish catches every song the stars are singing.
